title: Enlarge buffer cache and align planner I/O costs to cut physical reads
configuration_cause: shared_buffers=16384 (128MB) is tiny versus 2.1TB RAM; blks_read_per_txn=1.51 vs blks_hit_per_txn=9.23 (~86% hit ratio) and effective_io_concurrency=1 with random_page_cost=4.0 make the planner overvalue physical I/O, inflating GetUserTweets terminal occupancy (0.885).
mechanism: The dominant GetUserTweets transaction (88.5% of terminal capacity) is read-bound: only ~9.2 buffer hits per 1.5 physical reads per txn signals a working set far exceeding the 128MB shared_buffers. Raising shared_buffers to 1GB retains hot tweet/follow pages, while raising effective_cache_size and effective_io_concurrency and lowering random_page_cost/seq_page_cost lets the planner prefer cached index paths and prefetch, reducing physical reads and per-transaction latency so more transactions complete per terminal-second.
query_effect: Cached index/table lookups for GetUserTweets and GetFollowers replace physical reads; planner favors index scans over seq scans.
expected_tps_effect: Increase successful_transaction_tps above 20596 baseline as GetUserTweets latency drops.
expected_latency_effect: Decrease GetUserTweets p95 and overall p95.

predictions.rationale: Larger cache retains hot pages, cutting physical reads.
Fewer physical reads lower dominant transaction tail.
Lower terminal occupancy per txn raises completed TPS.

alternatives.statement: If the working set already fits and reads are index-only, larger shared_buffers yields no read reduction and TPS stays flat.
If planner cost changes alone drive the gain, blks_read stays flat while GetUserTweets p95 falls.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent leaves the mandatory buffer_cache_capacity bundle untested; low_buffer_hit_ratio is active and shared_buffers is uncovered. A coherent cache+planner action directly targets the read-bound dominant transaction.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 1GB = 131072*8kB, 8x current, well within 8192-65536... safe_high 65536 (512MB); choose 65536 to stay in bound
slight decrease within 0.5-2.0 to keep ratio sane
knob_changes.mechanism_role: I/O cost scale paired with random_page_cost

edges.relation: raises cache hit ratio and lowers physical reads
lower per-txn latency raises completed TPS

cross_domain_requirements: wal_commit_path bundle remains untested; wal_wait anomaly may need separate WAL-group action
